title: The seventh week
subtitle: The visit is behind you and the baby is starting to have a rhythm. Not a schedule. A rhythm.

baby.development: Your baby is batting at toys, bringing hands to the mouth on purpose, and holding their head steadier. They may laugh out loud for the first time this month.

you.body: If you are cleared for exercise, start with walking and core breathing. If you are breastfeeding, supply is usually established and engorgement is rare now.
you.mind: The help has gone home and the baby is more awake. This is the week a lot of people realize they have not eaten a proper meal in days.

coreActions.title: Start a bedtime routine, not a bedtime
coreActions.why: A short, repeated sequence is what teaches a baby that sleep is coming. The time on the clock matters less than the order.
coreActions.detail: Three or four steps, the same every night: feed, bath or wipe, sleep sack, dark room, a song. Ten minutes is enough. Do it at the same time each night and the baby starts to anticipate it.

coreActions.title: Eat something with protein at every meal
coreActions.why: Feeding a baby burns calories, and skipping meals is what turns tired into shaky.
coreActions.detail: Eggs, beans, yogurt, cheese, leftover meat, peanut butter. A handful of nuts counts. If someone offers to bring food, say yes and ask for something you can eat one-handed.

coreActions.title: Offer a bottle once a week if you may return to work
coreActions.why: A baby who has never taken a bottle can refuse one outright at eight weeks, and that is a hard week to discover it.
coreActions.detail: Offer a small amount of expressed milk in a bottle at a time when the baby is calm, not starving. Someone else gives it, ideally not in the room where you feed. Once a week keeps the skill.

alsoKnow.title: There is no regression at seven weeks
alsoKnow.body: The word gets used for every change in sleep. At this age sleep is still developing, and a bad week is usually a growth spurt or a developmental leap, not a step backwards.

alsoKnow.title: Breastfed babies need vitamin D
alsoKnow.body: 400 IU a day from birth. Formula-fed babies get it from the formula. It comes as a drop, and it is the one supplement a breastfed baby needs.

redFlags.text: A fever of 100.4°F or higher in a baby under three months
Refusing feeds, or far fewer wet diapers than usual
Feeling hopeless, or thoughts of harming yourself or the baby

sources.title: A parent's guide to safe sleep
